candidates.suggested_collection_method: Keyword-monitor the national and regional Policie ČR news feeds for 'bankomat', 'výbuch bankomatu', 'převoz peněz', 'ceniny'; geocode incidents and build an incident time series; corroborate with mainstream media coverage.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs-language search on ATM attacks and police statistics
queries_used: policie ČR útok na bankomat vytržení výbuch tisková zpráva statistika

candidates.source_name: KPKB ČR – Komora podniků komerční bezpečnosti ČR (kpkbcr.cz) and allied security associations
candidates.why_relevant: Sector chamber for commercial security businesses (founded January 1993) with corporate and individual member directories, a magazine, guard-qualification exam material and downloadable organisational documents. Cash-in-transit in Czechia is legally and operationally part of the commercial-security industry, so this chamber and its partner bodies (Česká komora služeb ochrany majetku a osob, Grémium Alarm, Česká asociace bezpečnostních manažerů, Hospodářská komora ČR) are the route to enumerating smaller and regional CIT/valuables-transport firms that no financial-sector list captures. Note: the partner page did not list Loomis/Brink's/Securitas, so membership coverage of the large CIT players is unconfirmed.
candidates.access_status: open_web
candidates.legal_status: association publication
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Harvest the member directories and partner list once, resolve each company to an IČO via ARES, then filter by CZ-NACE and self-described services to isolate firms doing převoz/zpracování cenin a hotovosti; re-check the directory annually.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs-language search for Czech security/CIT trade associations; direct fetch of the partners page
queries_used: Komora podniků komerční bezpečnosti ČR asociace bezpečnostních služeb převoz cenin

candidates.source_name: Diebold Nixdorf Czech Republic (dnpilsen.cz / Diebold Nixdorf s.r.o.) and other self-service vendors with Czech operations
candidates.why_relevant: The vendor layer beneath the Czech self-service estate. Diebold Nixdorf runs a substantial Czech operation (a Pilsen global centre, several hundred staff per its recruitment material) and Diebold Nixdorf s.r.o. is a registered Czech entity; NCR/NCR Atleos and legacy Wincor Nixdorf equipment is also present in the field. Vendor sites, Czech job postings and the local entity's own statutory filings are the practical way to read service-contract scale, managed-services push and which technology generation the Czech fleet is on — none of which appears in bank or deployer disclosures.
candidates.access_status: open_web; recruitment content on jobs.cz is open
candidates.legal_status: corporate and recruitment content
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Track the Czech vendor entity via ARES + Sbírka listin for revenue/headcount; monitor Czech job listings as a capacity/technology signal; cross-check vendor model names against the ČNB tested-device lists to see what is actually approved for the Czech market.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs/en-language search for ATM vendors with Czech presence
queries_used: NCR Atleos Diebold Nixdorf Česká republika bankomaty dodavatel samoobslužné technologie

candidates.source_name: Czech crypto-ATM operators and manufacturer (General Bytes, Bitperia, CryptoATM, bitcoinmaty.cz)
candidates.why_relevant: An adjacent but genuinely relevant part of the Czech self-service cash ecosystem: a domestic manufacturer/operator base (General Bytes, described in Czech media as among the world's largest producers and operators of bitcoin ATM infrastructure, and reported hacked in 2023) plus operating networks (Bitperia, CryptoATM, bitcoinmaty.cz). These machines compete for the same high-footfall cash-accepting sites as bank and deployer ATMs, are a live cash-in/cash-out channel, and are the population most exposed to incoming AML/MiCA-driven registration duties — a regulatory front that will reshape non-bank self-service in Czechia.
candidates.access_status: open_web
candidates.legal_status: commercial websites and copyrighted journalism
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Low-frequency monitoring of operator site machine-location lists and Czech tech media (cc.cz, e15.cz, iDNES) for network size, incidents and regulatory changes; resolve operators to IČO via ARES for filings.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs-language search for crypto ATM operators and General Bytes
queries_used: bitcoinmat kryptomat Česko provozovatel síť General Bytes

candidates.source_name: Česká pošta, s.p. – cash and payment services at post offices (incl. cash withdrawal) and annual reports
candidates.why_relevant: Czech Post is a large non-bank cash-access and cash-handling network (SIPO, poštovní poukázky, the ČSOB Poštovní spořitelna counter partnership, and a cash-withdrawal-from-account service), and as a state enterprise it publishes annual reports and appears in the public contracts register. Its counter network is the main substitute channel when bank branches and ATMs are withdrawn from small municipalities — the same demand gap Euronet targets with its 'ATMs for obce' offer — so its service and pricing changes are a leading indicator for deployer opportunity.
candidates.access_status: open_web
candidates.legal_status: state enterprise public information
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Track the payment/financial services pages and the price list for service and fee changes; pull the annual report PDFs; cross-check Registr smluv for its cash-transport supplier contracts.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs-language search on Czech Post cash services and annual reports
queries_used: Česká pošta hotovost cash služby bankovní přepážka výroční zpráva

candidates.source_name: ATM location directories and POI datasets (banky.cz, Mapy.com/OSM, Firmy.cz)
candidates.why_relevant: The only practical bottom-up way to size and profile the Czech ATM estate by operator, since neither ČNB (bank-operated only) nor SBK (stale) publishes a deployer-level breakdown. banky.cz maintains per-bank ATM listings with addresses; Mapy.com and Firmy.cz carry large numbers of individually tagged 'Bankomat Euronet' and bank ATM POIs (including OSM-sourced entries), which supports operator-mix and regional-density estimates and detects new deployments and removals over time.
candidates.access_status: open_web; OSM-derived POIs are openly licensed, portal-compiled listings are not
candidates.legal_status: mixed — OSM data under ODbL (attribution/share-alike); banky.cz and Firmy.cz/Mapy.com compilations are proprietary, so respect robots.txt and avoid bulk extraction
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Prefer OpenStreetMap extracts (amenity=atm with operator tags) as the licensed backbone for operator-level counts; use banky.cz per-bank listings and Mapy.com/Firmy.cz entries only as sampled corroboration; recompute operator mix quarterly.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs-language searches on ATM maps/directories and on independent ATM networks
queries_used: Česká bankovní asociace standard API bankomaty pobočky open data lokality
nebankovní bankomat nezávislá síť bankomatů Česko konkurence Euronetu

candidates.source_name: Česká bankovní asociace (cbaonline.cz) and ČBA Monitor
candidates.why_relevant: The Czech Banking Association publishes surveys, indices and sector positions, and ČBA Monitor carries sector data. For this cell it is a secondary but useful channel for branch/ATM accessibility positions, cash-availability policy debate and fraud statistics that contextualise self-service investment; it is also the natural venue in which any industry-level position on shared ATM infrastructure or cash access obligations would be voiced.
candidates.access_status: open_web
candidates.legal_status: association publications
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor the articles feed and the 'Průzkumy a indexy' section; filter for bankomat/hotovost/dostupnost; treat as commentary rather than primary fleet data.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs-language search for the Czech Banking Association and cash/ATM statistics
queries_used: Česká bankovní asociace cbaonline statistiky hotovost bankomaty

negative_findings.description: The WebSearch tool reported its per-session budget fully consumed (200/200) before this cell's first query, so all discovery had to be routed through WebFetch against public search engines. DuckDuckGo (html and lite endpoints) returned an anti-bot CAPTCHA challenge, which I did not attempt to solve, and Mojeek returned HTTP 403. Seznam.cz (search.seznam.cz) fetched successfully and became the sole discovery engine for this slice.
negative_findings.result_summary: All 16 discovery queries in this slice were executed through search.seznam.cz via WebFetch; ~10 results per query, first page only. No Google/Bing/DuckDuckGo coverage and no deep result pages.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Seznam's index is strong for Czech-language consumer and corporate content but weaker for English-language financial disclosure, PDF-embedded content and international trade press. Sources findable only via Google/Bing (e.g. ATMIA and international cash-industry publications, English-language CEE ATM market reporting) are systematically underrepresented in this slice, and no result set went past page one.

negative_findings.description: Targeted Czech-language searching for a non-bank ATM deployer other than Euronet ('nebankovní bankomat', 'nezávislá síť bankomatů Česko', 'konkurence Euronetu', 'provozovatel bankomatů', 'nezávislý provozovatel bankomatů v obcích') surfaced no second independent deployer of any scale. Results returned only Euronet properties, Euronet fee criticism, bank ATM listings and map POIs.
negative_findings.result_summary: No Czech IAD competitor to Euronet identified. Euronet's own June 2026 statement — ~10% of all Czech ATMs, ~300 of ~1,200 machines in Prague — is currently the only quantified deployer-share figure found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If confirmed, the Czech independent-deployer market is effectively single-operator, which concentrates the entire non-bank ATM intelligence problem on one company and its parent filings, and makes the Sbírka listin filing of Euronet Services (IČO 25608452) disproportionately important. It also means fleet-share claims come from an interested party with no rival source to triangulate against.

negative_findings.description: The status of G4S's Czech cash business could not be resolved. brinks.cz publishes a post about a partnership with 'G4S Secure Solutions (CZ) a.s.' framed as a security-services cooperation, and two Brink's cash entities are registered in Czechia (Brink's Cash Solutions (CZ) a.s., IČO 27590151, incorporated 2006-09-01; Brink's Cash Solutions Services (CZ) s.r.o., IČO 08829969, incorporated 2020-01-08, the latter's incorporation date being consistent with a carve-in around the Brink's–G4S cash transaction period). No document was found confirming whether G4S's Czech cash-in-transit operation was transferred to Brink's, retained, or wound down.
negative_findings.result_summary: G4S Cash Solutions as a distinct Czech CIT operator was not located; only G4S Secure Solutions (CZ) a.s. appears, as a Brink's partner in guarding-type services. Relationship unconfirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Whether the Czech CIT market is a two-player (Loomis/Brink's) or three-player structure changes any read on pricing power and on bank outsourcing leverage. Getting this wrong would misstate the competitive baseline for the entire cash-logistics side of this cell.

negative_findings.description: Sdružení pro bankovní karty (bankovnikarty.cz), historically the canonical publisher of total Czech ATM counts covering the whole estate rather than only bank-operated machines, shows detailed statistics only through roughly 2011–2012 on its Czech market profile page, despite the page carrying a recent 'aktualizováno' stamp.
negative_findings.result_summary: Latest detailed series observed: 10.03m cards, 4,082 ATMs, 69,878 merchant locations, 59,836 POS terminals, with trend data spanning 2001–2011.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This removes the one industry series that historically counted all ATMs regardless of owner. It is the direct cause of the fleet-attribution gap in this cell: ČNB counts bank-operated ATMs only, so without SBK there is no authoritative published split between bank-owned and deployer-owned machines.

negative_findings.description: No published ČNB list of persons authorised to process domestic banknotes and coins (a register of cash-processing companies) was located. The ČNB legislation section yields the Act on the circulation of banknotes and coins, professional-course requirements and the tested-device lists, and portal.gov.cz documents an information-provision duty toward ČNB, but no public roster of processors was found.
negative_findings.result_summary: Found instead: two device registries (banknote and coin processing equipment) and a gov.cz service page describing reporting to ČNB. No entity-level register of cash processors surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A processor register would be the cleanest possible census of the Czech cash-handling industry, including small and regional operators invisible to media and to financial-sector lists. Its absence forces reliance on CZ-NACE sweeps in ARES and on security-industry association directories, both noisier.

negative_findings.description: Four fetches failed and are recorded as hypotheses, not verdicts: ir.euronetworldwide.com (landing page and /news-events/press-releases) and investors.brinks.com both timed out at 60s; smlouvy.gov.cz search UI timed out at 60s; www.sec.gov EDGAR browse-edgar returned HTTP 403.
negative_findings.result_summary: None of these was confirmed dead. The SEC 403 is the expected response to a request without a compliant declared User-Agent under SEC access policy; the timeouts are consistent with CDN/bot defence or slow server-side rendering. smlouvy.gov.cz content was independently observed as indexed and reachable via search results (individual contract URLs appeared).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These four are among the highest-value disclosure endpoints in the cell. Recording them as dead would wrongly drop parent-level and contract-level intelligence; the correct next step is a fetch with a declared User-Agent and longer timeout, or use of the documented APIs and open-data dumps rather than the web UIs.

negative_findings.description: No Czech-language term, association or portal specific to cash-in-transit or ATM deployment as an industry was found. Searches on 'převoz cenin', 'komora podniků komerční bezpečnosti', 'asociace bezpečnostních služeb' returned only the general commercial-security chamber KPKB ČR and allied bodies, whose published partner list did not include Loomis, Brink's, G4S or Securitas.
negative_findings.result_summary: Czech CIT appears to have no dedicated sectoral association or trade portal; it sits inside the broader commercial-security industry vocabulary ('ostraha majetku a osob', 'převoz cenin', 'bezpečnostní služby').
negative_findings.why_it_matters: There is no single local-language hub to snowball from for cash logistics, so actor discovery for smaller CIT firms must come from CZ-NACE sweeps in ARES, procurement award notices and security-association member directories rather than from an industry body.

negative_findings.description: No Czech Banking Association API standard or open-data feed for ATM and branch locations was found. Searching in Czech for 'standard API bankomaty pobočky open data lokality' returned only consumer directories (banky.cz, penize.cz, airbank.cz map pages), with the engine explicitly flagging that results did not contain the API/association/open-data terms.
negative_findings.result_summary: No PSD2-style or association-standard ATM-locator open dataset located for Czechia in this run.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A standard locator feed would give exact, operator-attributed fleet data at near-zero collection cost. Without it, fleet mapping falls back to OpenStreetMap extracts and sampled directory scraping, which are less complete and carry licensing constraints.

negative_findings.description: No bank–ATM operator outsourcing contract or announcement was found in Czech-language searching ('banka outsourcing bankomatů smlouva Euronet MONETA Raiffeisenbank provoz sítě'). Euronet markets 'Outsourcing bankomatů' and 'Dohoda o účasti v síti' on its own /banky/ page, but no counterparty bank was named in any public source located.
negative_findings.result_summary: Outsourcing offer confirmed on the deployer side; no named Czech bank counterparty found in public sources.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Bank-to-deployer outsourcing is the single most consequential structural variable in this cell — it determines how much of the bank fleet is really deployer-run. That it is undisclosed on both sides means it must be inferred indirectly (Sbírka listin narratives, related-party notes, procurement records, field observation of operator branding on machines).

coverage_gaps.description: There is no public source that splits the Czech ATM estate by owner/operator. ČNB reports only ATMs operated by Czech banks (4.9 thousand at end-2025); Euronet self-reports ~10% of a ~5,000 machine national total; SBK's whole-estate series stopped around 2011. The three cannot be reconciled without an operator-attributed dataset.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a derived fleet-attribution estimate: take the ČNB bank-operated series as the denominator anchor, add an OpenStreetMap amenity=atm extract with operator tags for operator mix, sample banky.cz/Mapy.com listings for corroboration, and reconcile annually against Euronet Services' Sbírka listin filing. Document the estimate's method and error bars explicitly rather than quoting Euronet's share claim as fact.

coverage_gaps.description: The core financial disclosures for every Czech actor in this cell (Euronet Services 25608452, Loomis Czech Republic 26110709, Brink's Cash Solutions (CZ) 27590151, Brink's Cash Solutions Services (CZ) 08829969) exist only as PDFs inside the court Sbírka listin — often scanned — and were not retrieved in this run. Chytrý rejstřík indicates 56 documents on file for Euronet Services alone.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Stand up a Sbírka listin harvesting pipeline: resolve IČO via ARES, enumerate document rows per company and year, download účetní závěrka / výroční zpráva / zpráva auditora PDFs, OCR scanned filings, and extract revenue, EBIT, headcount, related-party balances and any narrative mention of bankomaty/síť/outsourcing. Backfill at least five years to establish trend.

coverage_gaps.description: Only the large, internationally-owned CIT operators were identified (Loomis, Brink's, plus the unresolved G4S question, and ČP Security surfaced incidentally as a money-transport provider). Smaller and regional Czech cash-transport and cash-processing firms were not enumerated, and no association directory covers them.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a systematic ARES sweep by CZ-NACE (security activities and auxiliary financial-service codes) combined with keyword matching on business-activity descriptions ('převoz cenin', 'přeprava a zpracování hotovosti'), then cross-check against KPKB ČR member directories and procurement award notices to build a full Czech cash-logistics actor list with IČOs.

coverage_gaps.description: Discovery in this slice ran on a single engine (Seznam.cz), first page only, because the WebSearch budget was exhausted and DuckDuckGo/Mojeek were blocked. English-language and international-trade-press coverage of the Czech ATM/CIT market is therefore thin in this slice, and no result set was paged beyond the first ten hits.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run this cell's query set on Google/Bing with a raised WebSearch budget, going at least three result pages deep, and add English-language queries targeting international cash-industry sources (ATM industry associations, CEE payments trade press, ATM/cash-handling market reports) plus site-scoped queries against euronetatms.cz, brinks.cz and cz.loomis.com for content not surfaced by Seznam.

coverage_gaps.description: Four high-value endpoints were not successfully retrieved — Euronet Worldwide IR, Brink's IR, SEC EDGAR (403), and the smlouvy.gov.cz search UI (timeout) — so parent-level segment disclosure and contract-level evidence remain unread for this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Retry with a compliant declared User-Agent and extended timeout; prefer machine interfaces over web UIs — SEC submissions/full-text-search APIs for EEFT and BCO, and the Registr smluv open-data dump filtered by supplier IČO — rather than repeatedly fetching the HTML front ends.

coverage_gaps.description: Bank-to-deployer ATM outsourcing and network-participation agreements — the variable that determines how much of the nominally bank-operated Czech fleet is actually run by a third party — are undisclosed by both banks and Euronet. Similarly, bank–CIT cash-logistics contracts are private and outside the public contracts register.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Attack indirectly and triangulate: mine Sbírka listin annual-report narratives and related-party notes for both sides; monitor Věstník veřejných zakázek, NEN and Registr smluv for any public-sector or state-controlled counterpart contracts as pricing benchmarks; track bank newsroom announcements for network participation; and consider a structured field-observation protocol recording operator branding and surcharge screens on sampled machines.

coverage_gaps.description: No long-run Czech time series for the deployer-operated ATM estate or for CIT market size was assembled. ČNB's series covers bank-operated machines from 2021 onward in the commentary text, SBK's whole-estate series ends around 2011, and CardMag's archive is unindexed PDF.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Reconstruct a joined series by harvesting the ARAD payment-statistics tables for the full available history, back-casting the pre-2012 whole-estate figures from SBK, and text-mining the CardMag PDF archive for interim-year fleet and operator references; document the splice points.

brief: Czech ATM and cash-handling intelligence rests on a narrow but high-quality base: Euronet is the only independent deployer of scale found (self-reporting ~10% of a ~5,000-machine national estate, ~300 of ~1,200 ATMs in Prague), while cash-in-transit is effectively a Loomis/Brink's duopoly, with the fate of G4S's Czech cash business unresolved. Because all three Czech operating entities are private subsidiaries with no local investor relations, their only recurring hard disclosure is the statutory účetní závěrka/výroční zpráva filed into the court Sbírka listin (confirmed live for IČO 25608452 and 26110709), backstopped by ARES for entity resolution and by parent-level reporting at Euronet Worldwide, Loomis AB and Brink's. Public-sector channels — Věstník veřejných zakázek, NEN and Registr smluv — are the only route to actual cash-logistics contract terms and pricing, since bank–operator agreements are disclosed by neither side. The critical structural weakness is fleet attribution: ČNB counts only 'bankomaty provozované českými bankami' (4.9k at end-2025, with withdrawals down to 140.4m transactions) and the SBK whole-estate series died around 2011, so the bank-owned versus deployer-owned split has no authoritative publisher and must be derived from ČNB anchors plus OSM/directory operator tagging.
